decision_thread_registry.title: Outbound correction cancellation and OTC3 execution

detection.summary: Public mission reporting established that Orion's trajectory remained sufficiently on track for earlier planned outbound corrections to be cancelled.

evidence.summary: Two planned outbound trajectory corrections were cancelled while OTC3 was later executed before lunar sphere-of-influence entry.

constraint.summary: Trajectory correction activity must balance the current flight solution with downstream lunar geometry and mission timeline.

options.summary: The complete set of alternatives, targeting thresholds, and console trade discussions is not public.

decision.summary: OTC1 and OTC2 were cancelled and OTC3 was retained and executed.

action.summary: OTC3 executed on 2026-04-06T03:03:00Z.

outcome.summary: The mission continued into the lunar encounter sequence. MissionLab derived lunar SOI entry at 2026-04-06T04:38:07.532302Z.

decision_thread_registry.title: Flight Day 1 toilet fault and in-flight recovery

detection.summary: Crew reported a blinking fault light during toilet-system checkout.

evidence.summary: Mission Control assessed available data and coordinated troubleshooting with the crew.

constraint.summary: The public evidence established a system fault indication but did not identify the failed component or root cause.

options.summary: Private troubleshooting branches and internal fault-isolation options were not publicly released.

decision.summary: The public sequence supports continued troubleshooting rather than abandonment of the system.

action.summary: Crew and Mission Control performed troubleshooting.

outcome.summary: Normal toilet operations were restored. The underlying root cause remained unavailable in the curated public source set.

detection.summary: Wastewater venting ended earlier than expected.

evidence.summary: NASA reported that the tank was not full, the toilet remained operational, possible ice was considered, and other causes were also under review.

constraint.summary: Waste-management capacity and continued crew operations had to be protected while the physical cause remained uncertain.

options.summary: NASA publicly described several responses but did not publish the complete internal option set or decision trade matrix.

decision.summary: The mission adopted a managed mitigation posture while continuing to investigate.

action.summary: Engineers used vent heaters, oriented the vent toward the Sun, reviewed other potential causes, and maintained backup collection capability if needed.

outcome.summary: The toilet remained operational and the mission continued. NASA's April 20 postflight assessment still described the urine vent-line root-cause investigation as ongoing.

decision_thread_registry.title: Expected lunar communications constraint and reacquisition

detection.summary: Lunar geometry created an expected period in which direct Earth communications were blocked.

evidence.summary: Earthset, lunar occultation geometry, Earthrise, and the communications sequence are mutually consistent.

constraint.summary: The lunar body physically blocked the direct line of sight between Orion and Earth.

options.summary: MissionLab treats the expected occultation as a planned geometric constraint rather than an anomaly requiring fault-response options.

decision.summary: Mission planning accepted the expected loss-of-contact window within the lunar-flyby sequence.

action.summary: The mission proceeded through the lunar-flyby observation sequence and later reacquired Earth communications.

outcome.summary: The expected communications constraint ended as Earth re-emerged from behind the Moon.

decision_thread_registry.title: Lunar science opportunity to confirmed observation

detection.summary: Preflight targeting identified science opportunities tied to lunar-flyby geometry.

evidence.summary: Postflight imagery, audio, crew annotations, and LRO context confirm observations of Earthset, Earthrise, terminator terrain, eclipse phenomena, and impact flashes.

constraint.summary: Observation opportunities were bounded by flight geometry, illumination, crew timeline, and available viewing conditions.

options.summary: The complete real-time science prioritization trade space is not reconstructed from public data.

decision.summary: The mission executed the public lunar observation program.

action.summary: Crew captured imagery, provided spoken observations, and produced annotations during the lunar sequence.

outcome.summary: Postflight science products document confirmed lunar observations, five impact flashes, coronal structure, zodiacal light, and selected terrain interpretations.

decision_thread_registry.title: Unexpected return-link loss, recovery, and RTC2 continuation

detection.summary: NASA reported an unexpected return-link communications loss before RTC2.

evidence.summary: Public reporting establishes the communications interruption, recovery, resumed burn preparation, and subsequent RTC2 execution.

constraint.summary: The communications condition had to be resolved sufficiently for nominal mission operations and burn preparation to continue.

options.summary: The complete fault-recovery option set and internal console discussion are not public.

decision.summary: Following communications recovery, burn preparation resumed.

action.summary: RTC2 executed at 2026-04-10T02:53:00Z.

outcome.summary: RTC2 was completed successfully and the return mission continued.

decision_thread_registry.title: Artemis I heat-shield finding to Artemis II mitigation and postflight outcome

detection.summary: Artemis I postflight inspection identified unexpected Avcoat char liberation.

evidence.summary: NASA's investigation linked low-permeability Avcoat, internal gas-pressure buildup, cracking, and the Artemis I skip-entry thermal history.

constraint.summary: The Artemis II heat shield was already integrated, requiring a flight-rationale and mitigation approach compatible with the existing spacecraft.

options.summary: NASA publicly described the engineering principle that the material or the entry environment could be changed to control the known mechanism.

decision.summary: For Artemis II, NASA changed the entry environment by flying a modified trajectory without the Artemis I-style skip entry.

action.summary: Artemis II executed the modified entry profile and completed atmospheric entry.

outcome.summary: Initial postflight assessment reported expected TPS performance and significantly reduced char loss. NASA technical reporting later described the Artemis II entry as successful.

decision_thread_registry.title: Final return correction to Entry Interface

detection.summary: The return trajectory entered its final publicly reported correction opportunity before entry.

evidence.summary: RTC3 occurred at 18:53 UTC and Entry Interface at 23:53 UTC.

constraint.summary: The final return state had to support the required transition into the entry sequence.

options.summary: Public evidence does not expose the complete targeting trade space, covariance, or final guidance decision thresholds.

decision.summary: RTC3 was executed as the final publicly reported trajectory correction before entry.

action.summary: The spacecraft proceeded through entry preparation and reached Entry Interface five hours later.

outcome.summary: The mission transitioned from return trajectory management into atmospheric entry.

decision_thread_registry.title: Planned entry plasma blackout and communications reacquisition

detection.summary: NASA expected communications loss shortly after Entry Interface as plasma developed around Orion.

evidence.summary: The public sequence reports Entry Interface, planned blackout, and communications reacquisition.

constraint.summary: The ionized plasma environment temporarily obstructed normal communications during atmospheric entry.

options.summary: The blackout is treated as an expected entry constraint rather than an unexpected fault requiring a reconstructed response tree.

decision.summary: The entry sequence proceeded through the expected blackout window.

action.summary: NASA later reported communications reestablished at the public 00:00 UTC minute.

outcome.summary: Contact was restored before the publicly reported parachute deployment sequence.

decision_thread_registry.title: Parachute descent, splashdown, and recovery transition

detection.summary: Following entry and communications reacquisition, Orion entered the publicly reported parachute descent sequence.

evidence.summary: NASA reported drogue deployment, all three main parachutes, splashdown, crew extraction, and spacecraft recovery.

constraint.summary: The sequence had to transition safely from atmospheric flight to water landing and maritime recovery.

options.summary: MissionLab does not reconstruct private recovery-team contingency decision trees or unreported parachute-response logic.

decision.summary: The public record shows the nominal descent and recovery sequence proceeding to completion.

action.summary: Drogues deployed, mains deployed, Orion splashed down, recovery forces approached, crew were extracted, and Orion was recovered.

outcome.summary: The crew and spacecraft were recovered, closing the flight phase and opening detailed postflight engineering analysis.

postflight_registry.summary: Orion recovery transitioned the mission from flight operations into spacecraft inspection and postflight engineering analysis.
NASA reported that initial Orion thermal-protection assessments found expected performance and significantly reduced Artemis I-type char-loss behavior.
NASA reported hardware assessment and data gathering were continuing to identify the urine vent-line root cause and support corrective action for a future mission.
NASA Ames reported continued postflight analysis of Mission and Fault Management logic performance during Artemis II.
NASA's updated Orion testing reference linked heat-shield permeability knowledge and Artemis II mitigation experience to future heat-shield manufacturing improvements.

NASA released the preliminary Artemis II lunar-science results and archive, resolving selected early observations including the five-flash postflight result and coronal / zodiacal-light interpretation.

unified_records.title: Artemis I heat-shield finding to Artemis II mitigation and postflight outcome
unified_records.summary: Artemis I postflight inspection identified unexpected Avcoat char liberation. NASA's investigation linked low-permeability Avcoat, internal gas-pressure buildup, cracking, and the Artemis I skip-entry thermal history. The Artemis II heat shield was already integrated, requiring a flight-rationale and mitigation approach compatible with the existing spacecraft. NASA publicly described the engineering principle that the material or the entry environment could be changed to control the known mechanism. For Artemis II, NASA changed the entry environment by flying a modified trajectory without the Artemis I-style skip entry. Artemis II executed the modified entry profile and completed atmospheric entry. Initial postflight assessment reported expected TPS performance and significantly reduced char loss. NASA technical reporting later described the Artemis II entry as successful.

unified_records.summary: The return trajectory entered its final publicly reported correction opportunity before entry. RTC3 occurred at 18:53 UTC and Entry Interface at 23:53 UTC. The final return state had to support the required transition into the entry sequence. Public evidence does not expose the complete targeting trade space, covariance, or final guidance decision thresholds. RTC3 was executed as the final publicly reported trajectory correction before entry. The spacecraft proceeded through entry preparation and reached Entry Interface five hours later. The mission transitioned from return trajectory management into atmospheric entry.

unified_records.title: Planned entry plasma blackout and communications reacquisition
unified_records.summary: NASA expected communications loss shortly after Entry Interface as plasma developed around Orion. The public sequence reports Entry Interface, planned blackout, and communications reacquisition. The ionized plasma environment temporarily obstructed normal communications during atmospheric entry. The blackout is treated as an expected entry constraint rather than an unexpected fault requiring a reconstructed response tree. The entry sequence proceeded through the expected blackout window. NASA later reported communications reestablished at the public 00:00 UTC minute. Contact was restored before the publicly reported parachute deployment sequence.

unified_records.title: Parachute descent, splashdown, and recovery transition
unified_records.summary: Following entry and communications reacquisition, Orion entered the publicly reported parachute descent sequence. NASA reported drogue deployment, all three main parachutes, splashdown, crew extraction, and spacecraft recovery. The sequence had to transition safely from atmospheric flight to water landing and maritime recovery. MissionLab does not reconstruct private recovery-team contingency decision trees or unreported parachute-response logic. The public record shows the nominal descent and recovery sequence proceeding to completion. Drogues deployed, mains deployed, Orion splashed down, recovery forces approached, crew were extracted, and Orion was recovered. The crew and spacecraft were recovered, closing the flight phase and opening detailed postflight engineering analysis.
